questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To me the study destination was not that important at first. I just wanted to go abroad to explore a new culture. Then I found out, that in Iceland, I could combine this with courses about Danish literature as well as the connection between Danmark and Iceland. In this sense, my courses became very much related to my studies at home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been an amazing experience to study abroad. I have learned a lot about my self and how to deal with a new culture and school system although it is similar to the danish school system. Also I have met so many cool people as well as I have used my English language a lot more.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find information. The university did help me a lot as I could both write them, if I didn't understand the information online, and they offered a great introduction online (due to COVID) in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived later than the official dates of the beginning of the semester, because I had an exam at home. Thereby I didn't have the chance to get assistance physically. When I arrived, everyone was very friendly and helped me creating a study card, get access to the portals etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I could either apply for a studio appartment where I could live by myself or a dormitory. I chose to live in a dormitory because I wanted to get to know some other students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We lived 13 people on a dormitory and we had to share a kitchen. We did not have much space, but we found a routine so everyone was able to use the kitchen facilities. At the same time we felt very good about each other hence why we sometimes prepared a meal and ate it together.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a really good way to get to know other exchange students. It can be a place, where a lot of parties takes place, which can either be a good or bad thing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registrated my courses at home, and when I arrived, I had to confirm my choice of courses. It was possible to change courses if you wanted to, but I did not, so it was a very easy process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always write an email and they would answer very quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I got all the courses I applied for at home.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I applied for at home. In the meantime I know a lot of students, who changed their courses after they arrived, and it was very easy. So don't be afraid to choose a course, because you can change it. Also, sometimes the courses applied for at home are not offered when you arrive, hence why you will need to re-registrate courses, but that is not a problem.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was a little bit lower than at my home university. Two of my courses were taught in danish, hence why it was easy for me to follow these courses. We had a lot of reading to to in those courses, but not many tasks. My third course was taught in english, and it was thereby more challenging for me, and there were more tasks.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. The big difference was the amount of people within the courses. Whereas we normally are about 25 students in a class at home, we were only 7 students in two of my courses here in Iceland. Therefor the teaching was even more dialogue based than at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Bilingualism 
2) Forholdet mellem Danmark og Island 
3) Skandinavisk samtidslitteratur

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both bilingualism and Skandinavisk samtidslitteratur

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When you move to another place, there will always be uexpected costs such as specific things for your room (to me it was for example a blanket and decorative pillows) and basic elements for the kitchen. Also, you can never know how much money you will spend on trips around the country, social events etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: tofu was super cheap and I used it a lot for my cooking. Besides that, almost all items in supermarkets were a lot more expensive than at home. On the other hand, some cultural events were cheaper than expected, as some of the museumentries were even for free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I used the school gym very much, and there is a student cellar with a lot of cool events. Other than that I bought a card for the local swimm, and used this a lot during my stay.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The gym and the pools! It is a nice way to get exercise and hang out with your friends at the same time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend renting a car in the weekends and go on roadtrips. It is not expensive if you can fill up a car, and there are so many magnificent places to see and experience around Iceland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Denmark and Iceland are very similar countries, and many groceries are from Denmark, as well as icelanders also know a lot of the danish language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was so lucky, that some icelanders also had the courses taught in Danish, and because we very so few student, we got to know each other very well. I know it can be difficult to get to know the local students when you are an exchange student, so I think - if you want to get to know the locals, you should participate in social events at campus and don't be afraid of reaching out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated how the icelanders are more 'loose' than in Denmark. Both within the school system and in the every day. The atmosphere is less busy and if you for example miss a deadline, you are now caught in the system, but instead they are understanding to human mistakes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) The academic expectations are less high 
2) It is a very small university - which I found pleasent - but it means that sometimes you are just a few students in a class 
3) Everyone is so nice and helpful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to meet new people, to practice my english language and to experience how to live in a foreign country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was challenging that everything was more expensive than at home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
